questions.question: Summarize the discussion about product appearance.
questions.reference_answer: The user interface designer put forward that the basic colour would be red and yellow and there would be two basic shapes - circle and triangle, which was called a mushroom design. Specifically, the prototype had 3 key features - a fuzzy look, a spherical channel selection and a stable triangle base. However, the marketing thought mushroom was not in the trends so the group decided to change it into a pineapple.

questions.question: Why did the user interface think the basic colour should be yellow and red when talking about the product appearance?
questions.reference_answer: Because yellow was their company colour and red was more attractive, which met the product requirement that the remote control should have a fancy look to attract the customers.

questions.question: Why did the marketing disagree with the user interface designer on the shape of the product when discussing product appearance?
questions.reference_answer: In the user interface designer's design, the shape of the product and the buttons were all mushrooms, but the marketing thought mushroom was not in the trends because mushroom was neither a vegetable nor a fruit.

questions.question: Summarize the discussion about product evaluation.
questions.reference_answer: The marketing suggested measuring how good the design was instead of just talking about it so the group started to judge the design in three aspects on a scale of one to seven, one being true and seven being false. The criterion was how fancy, technologically innovative, and easy-to-use the remote control was and it got three, two, and four in separate aspects, which meant it was acceptable.

questions.question: Why did the group think the design was technologically innovative?
questions.reference_answer: The controller had an embedded microphone array which could recognise simple vocal commands and the four microphones could capture voice from different directions. It also had tactile buttons, which was a really good point.

questions.question: Why did the marketing and the industrial designer disagree with the user interface designer when judging whether the controller was easy to use?
questions.reference_answer: The user interface designer thought it was easier than a traditional controller because you didn't have to press a button, just turn the ball to a certain angle to select channels. However, the marketing and the industrial designer thought it was quite difficult because users didn't know the angle was the correct one and they had to go through all the channels if they wanted to jump from channel one to twenty.

questions.question: Summarize the discussion about industrial design and quotation.
questions.reference_answer: The group decided that the product would have a low level chip, one button with LCD, a scroll wheel with a push button on it, a battery in the base, a single curve, and solar cells and it would be plastic instead of wooden so that the costs were 12.5 Euros which was within the budget. Furthermore, they came up with some new ideas about future products, such as a fruit collection of electronic devices or a customizable TV that followed the trend and people's moods.

questions.question: Why did the group decide to keep the solar cells when discussing the industrial design?
questions.reference_answer: Although solar cell was the most expensive part of the whole product, it still played a crucial role in making the controller technologically innovative. Plus, it would be interesting for their marketing team to make a lot of advertisements to sell it.

questions.question: Why did the industrial designer disagree with the marketing when talking about some new ideas about future products?
questions.reference_answer: The marketing thought they should not trust too much the trend because it wouldn't last long - fruits and vegetables were in fashion this year but maybe next year it would be insects. However, the industrial designer believed it was good to follow the flow now and then since electronic devices were not long life products: if people changed, the product appearance should change as well.
